newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses end down, hit by Wall St drop.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses end down, hit by Wall St drop.

text.p: European bourses ended down on Friday, buffeted by Wall Street which fell one percent as fresh U.S. economic data added to fears of higher interest rates.
The Dow Jones industrial average lost more than 50 points at Friday's start after Commerce Department figures showed new orders received by U.S. factories climbed strongly during July.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar was slightly down against the mark in late European trade in quiet business as U.S. dealers made an early start to the Labor Day weekend.

London, Frankfurt and Paris, reeling from losses during the day after New York closed down overnight 1.13 percent, plunged further when New York fell 55.11 points at 5592.54 within minutes of the start on Friday.
The robust factory orders data was followed shortly by figures showing more signs of economic growth, an unexpected jump to 60.0 in the Chicago Purchasing Managers index (PMI).
Concern about a strengthening U.S. economy is expected to make the market increasingly nervous in the lead up to Friday's key U.S. jobs data, seen as a determinant of future monetary policy.
"Of all major markets, the UK market provides the best combination of values, but it can't withstand a sustained decline in U.S. markets," said one trader.

"Sentiment has been very, very volatile in the past few months. In the last couple of weeks we've seen a revival of the bearish case that U.S. interest rates will have to go up," said Credit Lyonnais Laing market strategist Corey Miller.
The bout of jitters helped London's FTSE index to close down 17.4 points at 3867.6.
In Frankfurt, equities followed Wall Street's plunge falling 0.56 on the computerised IBIS index after floor trading ended down 0.63 percent.
Traders said that market players were winding up positions in advance of U.S. long weekend, when American markets are closed and volumes in Frankfurt are expected to be low.

"Even though we took a hit after last night's close on Wall Street, I still think the German share market is proving remarkably resilient to U.S. data -- we haven't seen a serious correction yet," said a Frankfurt trader.
French stocks ended down 0.35 percent after shedding 1.27 percent on Thursday on worries about the prospect of industrial unrest in the autumn.
A drop of 20,000 in French July unemployment, announced on Friday, and a continuing trade surplus in June, albeit slightly reduced from May, gave some comfort to investors.
The franc strengthened to 3.4239 against the mark in late trading after hitting a five-month low of 3.4296 against the German currency on Thursday.
The dollar was unsettled by the weaker U.S. Treasury and Wall Street and drifted lower in late European business.
The dollar was at 1.4795 marks well down on the day's high and on Thursday's close at 1.4815.
"The data will add to the concerns over the strength of the U.S. economy," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.
"The dollar has failed to gain much ground so far, and the upside may be limited if the market starts to believe that the Fed is behind the curve."
Comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer that U.S. fundamentals should allow a slightly higher dollar helped underpin the U.S. currency earlier today.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 108.67 yen and 1.4795 marks, compared with 108.50 and 1.4815 in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 17.4 points lower at 3,867.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 6.95 at 1,970.61.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 16.23 at 2,543.83.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $386.35, compared with Thursday's close of $388.25. Silver finished at $5.16, down six cents.
